meta.cv: GroupKFold on Bemis-Murcko scaffolds (identical to A-001/A-005/A-006)

H12_leakage_demonstration.target: sTDA computed gap  E_S1 - E_T1  (the quantity a leaked study regresses on)

leaked_features.description: 35 NTO spatial descriptors PLUS the S1 and T1 energy scalars

energy_free_features.description: the same 35 NTO spatial descriptors, energies excluded

H12_leakage_demonstration.note: Both cross-validated on the same Bemis-Murcko scaffold GroupKFold(5) as the rest of the study. The contrast between the two rows IS the leakage demonstration. Learner choice matters: a random forest is axis-aligned and cannot represent a difference of two continuous inputs, so it UNDERSTATES the leakage; a linear model recovers the identity exactly. The leakage claim is about recoverability, so the linear row is the honest demonstration.

flat_protocol.description: every learner scored on the identical outer folds; the best is reported

nested_protocol.description: learner selected inside each training fold, scored on the untouched outer fold

H3_nested_cv.note: positive selection_optimism = the flat protocol was optimistic by that many eV
